page.layout: One printed page, numbered 73. Running head "ITALIA." at top. Main text in one full column of verse and headings. Marginal notes in the right margin, with a catchword-free foot. A short note "Baiae." at top right beside the first line.

main_text.p: Quorum hominum regio, & qualis via: nam mihi Baiæ. Baias

p.i: Musa superuacuas Antonius: & tamen illis
Me facit inuisum, gelida cum perluor unda
Per medium frigus.
Eripe me his inuite malis: aut tu mihi terram Virgil. lib. 6. Æneid. Portus Velix.
Iunce (nanque potes) portúsque require Velinos.
Iamque adeo Scopulos Sirenum aduecta subibat,
Difficiles quondam, multorumque ossibus albos.

main_text.head: Anxur vrbs Volscorum.

p.i: Siue salutiferis candidus Anxur aquis.
Ora, manúsque tua lauimus Feronia lympha.
Millia tum pransi tria repsimus, atque subimus
Impositum saxis late candentibus Anxur.

main_text.head: Feronia.

p.i: Ora, manúsque tua lauimus Feronia lympha.
Dives vbi ante omnis colitur Feronia luco,
Et facer humectat fluuialia rura Capenas.
Fama est, intactas longævi ab origine Fauni
Creuisse in medium, congestis undique donis
Immensum per tempus opes, lustrísque relictum
p.note: In Luco Feronia thesauri deponebatur, & seruabantur.

p.i: Innumeris aurum, solo seruante pauore.

main_text.head: Prænestæ.

p.i: Vester, Camœna, vester in arduos
Tollor Sabinos: seu mihi frigidum
Prænestæ, seu Tibur supinum,
Seu liquida placuere Baiæ.

page.notes: The "Baias" line at the top appears to be a catchword or running fragment of the line above. Marginal notes on the right are reproduced where legible; some are partly faded. Words such as "inuisum" and "Iunce" are uncertain.
